swiperSeparability.verdictDetail: Embedded inside the shared vendor chunk sc0026.8ee1e431b3de.js = webpack chunk 2924. Both swiper core (module 2544 @104980) and swiper/react (module 2546 @92292) are modules inside that chunk, which also contains ~37 other unrelated modules (MUI Modal/Portal/Backdrop etc). There is no standalone swiper.js file in the capture. A secondary consumer layer is split across sc0027 (Carousel wrapper 3640) and sc0028 (call sites), so if you count consumers the shape is B-with-D-flavoured consumers; the LIBRARY itself is squarely B.
swiperSeparability.rationale: Chunk-header proof: sc0026 begins `(self.webpackChunk_N_E=...).push([[2924],{8442:function(...)` and module ids 2544/2546 are defined at offsets 104980/92292 within it. Extracting Swiper would mean carving two webpack module factories out of a 166KB chunk and re-providing their `r(7294)` React dependency plus the webpack `r.d`/`r.n` runtime.
swiperSeparability.independentOfReactRationale: Swiper is consumed exclusively through its React wrapper, and the wrapper is what creates the DOM. (1) The only Swiper entry points referenced by app code are `b.tq`/`b.o5` = the forwardRef React components from module 2546; module 2546 requires react (7294) and uses useState/useRef/useEffect/Children.toArray. (2) Module 2546 RENDERS the .swiper / .swiper-wrapper / .swiper-slide elements itself (`tag="div", wrapperTag="div"`) - it does not attach to pre-existing markup. (3) Every Swiper option that defines the behaviour (loop:true, autoplay{delay:5000,disableOnInteraction:true}, centeredSlides, spaceBetween, slidesPerView) is passed as React PROPS and appears nowhere in the rendered DOM - there is no data-swiper-* config attribute to recover them from. (4) slidesPerView is computed at render time from MUI useMediaQuery (`Q||(y?3:1)`), so it is React-state-derived. (5) The instance handles are captured via `onSwiper` into React refs and then used by sibling React components (prev/next buttons, the progress-indicator width useEffect, the hero <video> orchestration) and written into a mobx store (`y.activeMainBannerIdx`). (6) The slide CONTENT is `.map()`ed from mobx observable arrays populated by axios. Reviving Swiper vanilla over the Phase-2 DOM would produce sliding pixels but would NOT restore the source behaviour: the indicator bar, prev/next buttons, keyboard arrows, video-driven advance and the active-index store binding all live in React.
swiperSeparability.partialPathCaveat: One honest nuance, stated without optimism: the Phase-2 preservation clone DOES already contain the full expected markup (4x .swiper + 4x .swiper-wrapper + 29x .swiper-slide, 38 swiper-classed nodes), and swiper core (module 2544) is itself framework-agnostic. So a NEW vanilla Swiper could be constructed over that captured DOM. That is a re-implementation with hand-guessed parameters, not a restoration of the source's Swiper behavior, and it recovers only the slide-to-slide motion of a frozen slide set. The evidence shows no clean separation.

swiperSeparabilityCorrection.verdict: B — Swiper embedded in shared vendor chunk 2924 (unchanged)
swiperSeparabilityCorrection.retracted: The claim that Swiper 'never looks at the document to find its slides' is FALSE. Swiper core queries the wrapper's DOM children by `.${slideClass}, swiper-slide` (sc0026@114250, @121382, @123683), and app code calls e.el.getElementsByClassName("swiper-slide") (sc0028@6887). Configuration is NOT guessed: it is present as bundle literals (sc0028@7124 autoplay delay 5e3 + loop; sc0027@43035 slidesPerView Q||(y?3:1); sc0027@42153 spaceBetween default 50).
swiperSeparabilityCorrection.survivingGrounds: Source behaviour still depends on a mobx store and React callbacks: onSwiper/onAfterInit/onSlideChange write refs + store (sc0028@8002); slidesPerView is chosen by useMediaQuery (sc0027@43035); progress bar, prev/next, keyboard and hero-video advance reach swiperRef.current from React siblings.
swiperSeparabilityCorrection.consequence: A vanilla Swiper over the frozen Phase 2 DOM is more viable than first reported — core can discover the preserved slides and parameters are recoverable as literals. It would still omit store-driven behaviour, so it is a reconstruction, not preservation.

replayStrategies.revisedFrom: B_FIRST — reversed after independent review (M1–M4), see 08-independent-review.md

A.name: Phase 2 runtime DOM + localized source JS (on a COPY of the accepted clone)
A.feasibility: HIGH relative to B: reuses the existing data-preservation-* activation channel; trackers stay neutralized by construction; no new transform system
blockers: Phase 2 preview server sends `content-security-policy: script-src 'none'` (src/preservation-clone/serve.ts) — must be relaxed for the experiment
variants served at /desktop/ and /mobile/, not a server root; publicPath /_next/ is root-relative
API calls go to an absolute cross-origin host; needs browser-level request routing (e.g. automation request interception), not a same-origin server or service worker

hydration over post-fetch DOM with empty stores: React 17 legacy hydrate deletes unclaimed DOM and inserts missing nodes but does not repair attribute/className mismatches — expected result is a MIXED DOM (carousel subtrees removed, stale swiper-slide-active / aos-animate / Swiper inline styles on surviving nodes)
A.proves: executionIndependence (boot signals) AND hydration survival, as two separately instrumented observables in one run

B.name: initial response document + localized CSS/assets + source JS
B.feasibility: LOWER: response.html carries live third-party tags (kakao.js, kp.js, karrot-pixel.umd.js, inline GTM/fbq/ChannelIO/Naver) and zero data-preservation-* attributes, so it needs a SECOND neutralize-and-localize pass — a second transform system
blockers: second transform system (conflicts with no-second-system rule)
same CSP, server-root and browser-level routing needs as A
B.remainingAdvantage: separates boot failure from hydration damage by construction — but A can instrument the two separately
